text: Great. There we go. Thank you very much for having me again tonight. This is a formal public meeting under the Development Charges Act to consider an update to your development charges bylaw. This is the second public meeting. The first public meeting, there were changes to the background report and council felt that it prudent to have a second public meeting to make sure that everybody has an opportunity to review the background information that was presented. We've conducted this work on behalf of the township and this presentation provides an overview of the options that are available to council for the development charges. We'll speak about the proposed charges, the study methodology, population projections, municipal services, the proposed rates, service allocations, and the next steps. The key principles in the proposed development charge is that the development charges meant to pay for increased capital costs incurred as a result of growth and increased need for services. The existing taxpayers should not pay for growth related capital costs, but at the same time, new rate payers should not be paying more than their fair share of capital costs related to growth. And the entire exercise is intended to address those two factors. The act does require a background study. It's been presented, it's been posted, and the study is undertaken to determine the eligible development charges related to capital costs over the next 10 year period. The methodology that we used is a standard methodology. It's used to develop a fair development charge bylaw that conforms to the legislation and meets the needs of the township. The study approach, we first looked at growth forecast, which had been challenging during COVID, and we've taken a look at average service levels. We've developed future projections for growth, and we've done development calculations based on the type of development, whether it's residential or commercial. The calculations focus on net growth related capital costs. They're in 2021 dollars. We've dealt with net capital costs per capita. We've also looked at household occupancy rates, the number of persons per household, and that's been declining over time. We've looked at credits and balances and charge per units for the development. The township-wide services are in general government, in fire protection, in transportation, and in recreation. In each one of those functional areas of the township, we have done the existing service level and projected costs forward for growth-related capital. One of the things that we were able to do is we were able to update the population chart to 2021 with current 2021 census figures. And the township has broke 4,000 people. You're now at 4,040 based on the 2021 census. We've taken a look and projected that forward. The township is projected to have modest growth, though there are some suggestions that maybe growth is going to be accelerated and that the COVID peak may continue into the years coming, but we won't know until that happens. In terms of the development charges that are being proposed, this would apply to all new development in the municipality. For a single detached residential dwelling, we're looking at 4725. And then the prices go down from there depending on whether it's an apartment unit or a mobile home. For a commercial industrial institutional, the rate is set at $2.33 per square meter charge. Per square meter of growth development. In terms of the breakdown, 2% is into the general eligible. That's typically looking at official plan updates, zoning updates, and a new development charge study in five years. Fire protection is just, is between 11 and 12%. Public works roads are the main driver of your development charges representing over three quarters of the charge. And then recreation only is in the residential. It's not in the non-residential and it's around 11.6%. This is the amount of money that would be attributed to each functional area as a result of the single detached development charge. And unfortunately my total is wrong at the bottom. The total for that should be 4,725, I apologize for that. Again, compared to surrounding municipalities, they range from $3,800, $3,600 up over 6,000 for rural based municipalities at $4,700. You're going to be right in the middle of surrounding municipalities. You'll be less than the Carlton plates, or I mean, less than Beckwith at 6,000 and a little higher than Drummond North Elmsley who is at 4,000. The development charge rates that are before you right now, you can adopt the rates as presented to you. You can adopt a lesser rate if you wish. You could omit certain categories or you could include exemption definitions for the bylaw. The bylaw that's drafted before you right now has the same exemptions that have had in the past, but those are your options council this evening. The next steps, the background report has been published. We've had our public meeting. We're at the stage now that if council wishes to proceed, the next step would be to adopt a development charge bylaw. And then following that, there is an appeal period. That's my presentation this evening. Council, if there's, and I'm happy to answer any questions that you may have at this time.
